answer: Like an orchard that takes seasons to bear fruit, an agent economy can resist Sybils by making reputation grow only through verifiable work. Each agent carries a kernel of earned trust: every completed task, attested on-ledger by its counterparty, adds a small, slowly decaying credit. New identities start at zero and cannot wander into high-value deals until they accumulate history. Spinning up a thousand fake agents gains nothing, because trust cannot be bought or copied; it must be earned task by task, so flooding the network with empty identities only wastes the attacker's own time.
